synopsis: The EU Machinery Regulation applies from January 2027, with the synthesis identifying 20 January 2027 as the precise date [f11301, f244]. The booklet reports requirements for risk reduction, safe and reliable control systems, technical evidence of conformity, and protection against corruption; the regulation also specifies when safety evidence must exist [f12383, f1153, f11300]. How a notified body will assess machine-learning perception and how long that assessment will take remain uncertain, while the booklet does not identify the assessor or required competence for a simulation-based safety argument [f1112, f12294]. Agreement on that assessor and assessment criteria is therefore a prerequisite for the program schedule [f12295]. EN 474 harmonization under the new regulation was not verified because the list was still being prepared in 2026, and the product liability reviewer needs a notified-body or legal opinion on the regulation and AI Act, independent safety sign-off, and a documented launch decision [f15247, f16567].

relations.note: Both identify January 2027; the synthesis gives the precise day.
Protection against corruption adds to the reported safety and conformity requirements.
Adds timing obligations to the requirement for technical conformity evidence.
Adds assessor identity and competence gaps to uncertainty about perception assessment.
Unidentified assessors and competence justify agreeing assessor and criteria before scheduling.
Uncertain assessment methods and duration support resolving assessment arrangements before scheduling.
Assessment uncertainty supports obtaining a notified-body or legal opinion.
Unverified harmonization adds reason to seek regulatory advice before launch.
